touches.text: Postgres itself is a host service, installed and upgraded by Recovery (6.3.5); Rescue when it won't start.

A remote box keeps its own database and syncs it with the home box's (6.3.7.4). Node rows are the same on every box; the sync fills the blanks a box holds open (4.3.1.5.1.1). WHY: the local copy is fast, and the sync is the backup.

Who holds tables: every table of learning is a tree in the memory model (4.3.1.5), owned by the librarian and delegated to the devices that learn. A table that is not learning is an exception and names why; the bus's message table is the first (5.5.3.4.1).
Knowledge: one list of nodes, owned by the librarian.

The memory model. Everything Cairn keeps as LEARNING in database memory is these five things, and only these. Logs, troubles, git records and a device's own state keep their own homes (4.3.2-4.3.4). WHY: one kind of access everywhere.
Nodes: one long list, id = row. Every tree indexes it; no tree owns a node, so several trees can index the same node in different ways.

A row number is the same on every box. Storing a memory first reserves its slot from the librarian on the home box (CAIRN_HOME_HOST, 6.3.7.4), so two boxes are never handed the same slot, and the slot stays reserved until the write is complete. If a box's list is shorter than the slot (eg it holds rows up to 100 and is handed 123 while a sync is bringing the rest), it adds the open slots in between as blanks, and the sync fills them in as it proceeds. WHY: node ids are in every link and blob pointer, so a row has to mean the same node everywhere.

conflicts.ticket_says: Syncs separate per-nexus tables (codemother_orient_nodes, chart_orient_nodes, etc.), each owned by a device
conflicts.why: Outline 4.3.1.5.1 specifies 'one long list, id = row' of nodes with 'no tree owns a node'—a single unified store. A single shared node list and separate per-owner tables are mutually exclusive architectures.
